subject: Medialink executive snapshot — buying checklist & risk toggles
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@medialink.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medialink.com>, Procurement <procurement@medialink.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: today's discovery call — next steps for exec review

Thanks again for the run-through today. High-level notes for my leadership team: Claire (CEO) and Raj (CISO) want a clear one-pager that pulls together business outcomes, primary risks, and what procurement will need to sign off (SOW vs PO, SOC2 evidence, contract term).

Top bullets I captured on our side:
- Core pain: inference cost volatility and unpredictable tail-latency impacting ML-driven customer features.
- Goal: pilot by Q3 with an SLA-backed path to production if performance and cost align.
- Data concerns: partial PII and residency requirements for EU customers (some data must remain in EU region).

Can you confirm the executive summary + buy checklist you mentioned and share any early cost run-rate estimates? Procurement is also asking for an initial mutual action plan they can review with legal next week.

Attachments: Medialink-Requirements-v2.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Claire Huang
CEO, Medialink
claire@medialink.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medialink.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medialink.com>, Procurement <procurement@medialink.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today's discovery call — next steps for exec review

Claire — thanks for pulling this together. Below is a concise executive snapshot and the buying checklist we committed to produce. I pulled Marissa and Aditya into the thread for procurement and technical-readout items.

Executive snapshot (1 paragraph)
Medialink is looking to stabilize ML feature latency and reduce per-token inference cost while maintaining strict data controls for EU traffic. Redwood can deliver a scoped Q3 pilot (dedicated pool or private deployment) with predictable throughput and controls for residency, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs. Pilot success criteria: p50 latency <200ms, tail p95 <600ms, accuracy parity on sampled prompts, and monthly cost within provided budget envelope.

Buying checklist (what procurement/leadership need)
- Decision owners: Claire (CEO - business sponsor), Raj (CISO - security/compliance), Alex Morales (Head of Engineering - implementation lead), Procurement (PO path).
- Forms of purchase: PO + SOW preferred; Dedicated reserved capacity contract if predictable throughput required; Private deployment for EU residency requirement.
- Security evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary, encryption-at-rest details, KMS/HSM integration checklist, data retention controls.
- SLA and exceptions: standard SLA applies; we can discuss a limited SLA addendum for pilot if necessary (exception requires VP approval).
- Timeline: 2-week legal review if using PO + standard SOW; 3–4 week timeline for Reserved capacity onboarding.
- Pricing ask we made: initial run-rate estimate (attached) and 90-day pilot pricing model.

Key risks & mitigations
- Risk: EU data residency adds deployment complexity — Mitigation: private deployment or EU-hosted dedicated pool with VPC peering.
- Risk: procurement timeline — Mitigation: provide a minimal SOW and a one-page commercial summary to accelerate PO.
- Risk: performance at scale — Mitigation: pilot with 10–20% production load and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant.

Attachments: redwood-cost-modeling.xlsx (xlsx), SOC2-snapshot.pdf (pdf), MAP-medialink-v1.xlsx (xlsx)

Next steps
1) I will send the one-page executive snapshot + MAP (attached) to you and Raj by end of day.
2) Aditya to prepare a short tech appendix on residency and KV-cache behavior for the CISO readout.
3) Procurement to confirm whether they prefer PO + SOW or a pre-filled order form.

Onwards — will follow up with a short factsheet for Claire to share with Alex and the procurement team.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood-cost-modeling.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medialink.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medialink.com>, Procurement <procurement@medialink.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today's discovery call — next steps for exec review

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 6:20 PM, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Executive snapshot (1 paragraph)
> Medialink is looking to stabilize ML feature latency and reduce per-token inference cost while maintaining strict data controls for EU traffic. Redwood can deliver a scoped Q3 pilot ...

Claire — adding a short commercial-oriented brief you can hand to the board or procurement. The language here is intentionally non-technical.

Commercial brief (for CEO/procurement)
- Outcome statement: Reduce inference unit costs and eliminate production incidents caused by tail-latency, enabling Medialink to expand ML-driven personalization without disproportionate infra spend.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: 1) <200ms p50, 2) cost ≤ projected run-rate (see attached model), 3) audit logs and KMS integration validated by Raj's team.
- Required docs for procurement: 1) One-page commercial summary, 2) SOC2 summary (we included a 2-page snapshot), 3) Draft SOW (we can provide a starter SOW for PO sign-off).
- Proposed pilot commercial terms: 90-day pilot, capped monthly spend for pilot, option to convert to Reserved Capacity with 30-day notice.

Program owner and escalation path
- Executive sponsor: Claire Huang (CEO) — primary sign-off for business outcomes.
- Security/technical sponsor: Raj Patel (CISO) — sign-off for residency and data handling.
- Redwood internal lead: Sean Gallagher (commercial), Aditya Rao (tech integration).
- Escalation: If pilot SLA or compliance exceptions are requested, escalate to Redwood VP of Product & Ops (Marissa to lead).

Please confirm the decision owners & whether procurement wants the draft SOW or a PO-first approach. If you prefer, we can produce both in parallel to shorten the calendar.

Thanks — attaching the MAP and the cost model we referenced.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(Attachment: MAP-medialink-v1.xlsx)

From: Claire Huang <claire@medialink.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medialink.com>, Procurement <procurement@medialink.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@medialink.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today's discovery call — next steps for exec review

Appreciate the concise summary, Sean and Marissa — this is exactly what Claire/Leadership needed. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the procurement sync next week:

1) Can you give a ballpark monthly cost for the 90-day pilot (capped) assuming ~100k tokens/day, mixed LLM workloads, and EU-residency for 25% of requests? We understand this can be a range — we just need something to include in the budget ask.
2) Data retention: our legal asks that logs with PII be deleted after 90 days unless we opt-in for longer retention. Can you confirm Redwood's retention controls and whether a shorter retention window is configurable for private deployments?
3) Contract term: procurement prefers PO + starter SOW. Please provide the starter SOW and the one-page commercial summary for them to review.

We will plan a procurement/tech sync for next Tuesday afternoon. Raj will lead the security checklist review; Alex will bring implementation timelines.

Thanks — attaching our updated requirements for reference.

Best,
Claire Huang
CEO, Medialink
(Attachment: Medialink-Requirements-v2.docx)
